metadata.title: Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane
metadata.abstract: The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $\pi$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.
metadata.comment: 7 pages, no figures. A foundational note on the fifth postulate, in contrast with Hilbert's neutral primitives. Keywords: parallel postulate, rectilinear plane, Hilbert's foundations, non-Euclidean geometry. Comments welcome

analysis.workSummary: 把 Lambert 四边形第四角为直角作为 rectilinear plane 的原始性质，再经矩形、三角形内角和与 Legendre 定理导出平行线唯一性，并比较另外两类平面。
analysis.breakthrough: 提供一套围绕等价欧氏性质展开的基础性表述。
analysis.limitations: 依据官方标题、摘要及作者评论的摘要级分析，尚未审读数学证明。作者明确不声称从其余四公设推出第五公设；对当前几何研究的新增定理贡献较有限。 AI 披露以独立全文核查记录为准。
analysis.priorityReason: 按与几何研究的关联、结论范围和可迁移方法安排阅读；作者明确不声称从其余四公设推出第五公设；对当前几何研究的新增定理贡献较有限。
analysis.lowPriorityReason: 以基础公理的重新组织为主，暂未看到面向当前几何前沿问题的实质性新工具或定理。
